requirements.title: BGT arguments are integer or BOZ bit sequences
requirements.definition: The I and J arguments to BGT shall each be of type integer or be a BOZ literal constant.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Future fixtures initialize scalar result variables or arrays to non-default, opposite, or otherwise load-bearing sentinels before calling the intrinsic and assert only exact logical, integer, kind, scalar-rank, or bit-sequence properties fixed by 16.9 and its 16.3/16.3.2 dependencies. Bit comparison plans use equality controls for the inclusive/non-inclusive operators and guarded BOZ literals with the leftmost bit set for the z-bit model length in use, deriving the bit sequence from 7.7 and the comparison from 16.3.2 without converting the BOZ literal to an integer value.

S16.9.46-001 intrinsics_16_9_e fixture: BGT accepts integer arguments as bit sequences; NOT(0) produces an all-one bit sequence that compares greater than one.
requirements.oracle_limitation:

Clause 16 argument shall-restrictions in these intrinsic sections are unnumbered program restrictions, so this packet records no local diagnostic facet for wrong argument type, argument class, or out-of-range POS; a future negative requires an independently numbered rule requiring rejection.
